name: Perplexity
shortDescription: AI search engine that answers with sources.
bestFor: Quick answers from the web with sources you can check
about: Perplexity is an AI search engine. You ask a question, it searches the web, and it writes an answer with numbered links to its sources, so you can check where each fact came from.
It is good for news, product research, comparing options and learning about a topic fast.
features: Follow-up questions in the same thread
Focus on academic papers, videos or discussions

howToUse.title: Open Perplexity
howToUse.text: Go to perplexity.ai or install the app. You can search without an account.

howToUse.title: Ask a full question
howToUse.text: Write it like you would ask a person: "What are the cheapest ways to send money from Dubai to Pakistan?"

howToUse.title: Check the sources
howToUse.text: Click the numbered links to see where each fact came from.

howToUse.title: Ask follow-ups
howToUse.text: Keep asking in the same thread to go deeper.

tips: Add a time, like "in 2026", for recent information.
Open at least two sources for anything important.
examplePrompt: Compare the best laptops under 150,000 rupees in Pakistan for a university student in 2026. Show a table of price, battery life and weight, with sources.
limitations: It can still misread a source. Check the links.
The free plan gives only a few Pro searches per day.
freePlanDetails: A few Pro searches per day.
pricingNote: US prices. App store prices in Pakistan may be different.

name: NotebookLM
shortDescription: Google's free AI notebook that answers questions from your own files.
bestFor: Studying from your own notes, books and PDFs, with podcast-style summaries
about: NotebookLM is a free tool from Google. You upload your own sources (PDFs, Google Docs, websites, YouTube videos) and it answers questions using only those sources, with links to the exact part it used.
It can also make an "Audio Overview": a podcast-style conversation about your sources, plus study guides, quizzes, flashcards and mind maps.
useCases: Study for exams from your notes
Listen to a podcast summary of a long report
Research from a set of documents
features: Answers only from your sources, with citations

howToUse.title: Sign in
howToUse.text: Go to notebooklm.google.com with your Google account.

howToUse.title: Create a notebook
howToUse.text: Make one notebook per subject or project.

howToUse.title: Add sources
howToUse.text: Upload PDFs, paste text, or add links to websites and YouTube videos.

howToUse.title: Ask questions
howToUse.text: Ask in the chat. Click the numbers to see the exact source.

howToUse.title: Make study material
howToUse.text: Generate an Audio Overview, quiz, flashcards or study guide.

tips: Add only good sources: answers are only as good as what you upload.
Listen to the Audio Overview while travelling to revise.
examplePrompt: Using only my uploaded lecture notes, make 15 multiple-choice questions for my exam with the answers and a one-line explanation for each.
limitations: The free plan has daily limits on chats and audio overviews.
It doesn't search the web unless you add sources.
freePlanDetails: 100 notebooks, 50 sources each, with daily limits.
cheapestPaidPlan: Higher limits with Google AI Plus — $4.99/month

name: Consensus
shortDescription: AI search engine for scientific research papers.
bestFor: Finding what scientific studies say about a question
about: Consensus searches millions of scientific research papers and summarises what they found. For yes/no questions, its "Consensus Meter" shows how many studies say yes, no or maybe.
It is useful for students, writers and anyone who wants evidence, not opinions.
useCases: Find studies for an assignment or thesis
Back up an article with evidence
features: Filters for study type and quality

howToUse.title: Ask a research question
howToUse.text: For example "Does sleep affect exam performance?"

howToUse.title: Read the summary
howToUse.text: Check the summary and the Consensus Meter.

howToUse.title: Open the papers
howToUse.text: Click the papers to read the details and cite them properly.

tips: Ask clear yes/no questions to get the Consensus Meter.
Use filters to see only larger or higher-quality studies.
limitations: Only research papers, so it is not for news or general questions.
Always read the paper before citing it.
freePlanDetails: Free searches with a limited number of Pro features.
pricingNote: US prices. Sources disagreed on the monthly price, so check the website.

name: Elicit
shortDescription: AI research assistant that finds papers and pulls data from them.
bestFor: Literature reviews: finding papers and putting their findings in a table
about: Elicit helps with academic research. It finds relevant papers for your question, summarises them, and can pull details, such as sample size or results, into a table so you can compare many studies.
It can also write research reports with citations.
useCases: Find papers you might have missed

howToUse.title: Ask your research question
howToUse.text: Write a specific question for best results.

howToUse.title: Choose papers
howToUse.text: Look through the found papers and keep the relevant ones.

howToUse.title: Add columns
howToUse.text: Add columns like "sample size" or "main finding" to extract details from each paper.

howToUse.title: Export
howToUse.text: Export the table to use in your review.

tips: Check extracted data against the paper: it can miss details.
Upload PDFs you already have to add them to the table.
freePlanDetails: Free searches with limits on extraction and reports.
pricingNote: US prices. Sources showed $10 to $12, so check the website.
